data.long_meaning: A person who is content, pleased, or finds joy in their surroundings and experiences. The name Riza carries the meaning “Contentment, Pleasure, Gladness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Turkish. data.cultural_impact: The name Riza is of Persian origin, meaning "contentment" or "satisfaction." In Persian culture, the concept of Riza reflects the capacity to find joy and peace within oneself and in one's surroundings. This name is commonly given to those who are believed to possess a strong sense of inner happiness and contentment.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic context, the name Riza holds a deeper spiritual significance. It is associated with the profound contentment and satisfaction that comes from embracing and surrendering to the will of Allah (God). The name also reflects the belief in the divine providence and living a purposeful life in accordance with His guidance. Ultimately, Riza serves as a reminder to always strive for inner peace and contentment through faith, worship, and good deeds.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Shahr Ashubah's 'Managib al-A'immah' states that Riza was the name of the fourth Imam of the Shia, Hasan al-Askari. He was born in Samarra, Iraq, in 260 AH (873 CE) and passed away in 260 AH (880 CE) during the Abbasid Caliphate. Riza is known for his hidden imamate, as he is believed to have designated his son, Imam Al-Mahdi, as his successor, who subsequently went into hiding and is believed to be living in occultation until the present day.

'Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah' by Ibn Babawayh al-Qummhi mentions Riza as the name of the eighth Imam of the Twelver Shia, Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir. He was born in Medina, Arabia, around 117 AH (735 CE) and passed away in Kufa, Iraq, in 132 AH (750 CE) during the Umayyad Caliphate. Riza is known for his extensive knowledge of Hadith and Fiqh, and he was a teacher and mentor to his son, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, who became the ninth Imam of the Twelver Shia.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Riza is a traditional Islamic name that has seen a resurgence in popularity in modern times. It is derived from the Arabic word meaning 'content' or 'satisfied'. The name Riza is seen as a nod to Middle Eastern culture and is often used as a modern, unique baby name. It has gained popularity on various platforms including Instagram, where it is used as a hashtag for beautiful Middle Eastern-inspired content, Pinterest, where it appears on boards dedicated to baby names and Middle Eastern culture, and BabyCenter, where it is a commonly searched and discussed name among expectant parents. The general trend is that Riza is seen as a beautiful and meaningful name, and is often chosen by parents who want to give their child a name with cultural significance.
